# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 27 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 27 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_027_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 2 — Simplicity and Giving

**1** He said to me, "Keep simplicity and be innocent, and you will be like children who do not know the wickedness that destroys the life of men. **2** First of all, speak evil of no one, nor listen with pleasure to one who speaks evil of another. But if you listen, you will share in the sin of the one who speaks evil, even if you yourself are without guilt — so guilty are you if you listen with pleasure to those who speak evil. **3** But slander no man, and speak well of all. Speak well of all men, neither adding to their sins nor taking away from their good qualities." **4** "Furthermore, do not be reluctant to give, and when you give, do not grumble; for you shall know who the good Rewarder of your giving is. **5** Give to all who are in need without discernment as to who deserves and who does not; give to all, for God wills that there be giving to all from his own gifts. Those who receive shall give account to God for why and for what they received; for those who receive in distress will not be condemned, but those who receive by hypocrisy will pay a penalty. **6** The giver is innocent, for just as he received from the Lord an instruction to give to all, so he must fulfill this service blamelessly. **7** Fulfill then this simplicity, and you shall live to God, and all who perform it will live to God."

---

*EMET note: Mandate 2 combines two themes: (1) freedom from slander/evil-speaking, and (2) undiscriminating generosity. The connection is "simplicity" (haplotēs) — the single-minded, undivided orientation that characterizes the innocent person.*
